chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abi Jameela, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The woman with vitiligo (barsha') and the insane woman and the leper woman can be returned [from the marriage]. I said, 'The blind woman?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'.

key_terms.الْبَرْصَاءُ: The woman with vitiligo (a skin condition causing loss of pigment)
key_terms.الْعَوْرَاءُ: The blind woman (or one with an eye defect)
key_terms.تُرَدُّ: She can be returned/rejected (in the context of marriage validity)
key_terms.وَالْمَجْذُومَةُ: And the leper woman (one with leprosy)
key_terms.وَالْمَجْنُونَةُ: And the insane woman (one with mental incapacity)

ai.seo_question: What physical defects allow a husband to return his wife in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* delineates the legal grounds for *khiyar al-‘ayb* (option of defect) in Shia jurisprudence, specifically identifying vitiligo (*barsa’*), insanity, and leprosy as valid reasons for returning a wife, while explicitly excluding blindness (*‘awra’*). This distinction highlights the scholarly focus on defects that significantly impact marital life or are visibly disfiguring, reflecting the nuanced application of fiqh principles in personal status law. The narration underscores the Prophet’s tradition as a primary source for deriving specific rulings on marital compatibility and consumer rights in marriage contracts.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziiyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Abu Jameela, from Zayd Al Shahaam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘She can be returned, the woman with vitiligo, and the insanity, and the leprosy’. I said, ‘The blind?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from abu Jamilah from Zayd al-Shahham who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Marriage of a woman with illness of al-Bars (albino), insanity and leprosy is revoked and invalid.’ I asked about a blind. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, it does not apply to her.’”
